# W10 requests (Datasets)

Changes W10 needs outside `internal/datasets`, `internal/api/datasets.go` and `compat/viewer`, for the integration lead to reconcile in phase 2. Each item gives the change, the reason and what W10 did in its branch.

## 1. `internal/datasets` interface changes (consumers: W4, W8, W9)

`internal/datasets/datasets.go` is W10's, but W4's `hfapi` and the UI build against it, so the changes are listed here. The fake in `datasetstest` follows them.

| Change | Reason |
|---|---|
| `Viewer.FirstRows` returns `*FirstRowsResponse` (`dataset`, `config`, `split`, `features`, `rows`, `truncated`) instead of `*RowsResponse`. | The Hub's `/first-rows` shape has no `num_rows_total` or `partial`. |
| `Row.Row` is `Cells`, an ordered list of `{Name, Value}` that marshals as a JSON object in feature order. | The Hub's rows keep the column order; a Go map sorts keys. Use `Cells.Get(name)` to read a cell. |
| `SplitsResponse.Pending` is `[]ConfigRef` and `Failed` is `[]FailedConfig` (`dataset`, `config`, `error`). `ParquetResponse` gains `Features` (one Config) and always writes `pending` and `failed` for a dataset. | The Hub's shapes. |
| `Config` gains `SplitOrder`, `Files` (the data files matched at the Commit) and `Features` (declared by the card). | `datasets` keeps the card's Split order; DATA-7, DATA-8 and DATA-12 need the concrete files. |
| New `datasets.FormatFloat`. | Floats as orjson writes them, shared by the Viewer and statistics. |

Smallest compatible edit: none possible for a changed return type; W4 changes `FirstRows` call sites to the new type (field names are unchanged where they overlap).

## 2. Wiring in `cmd/hangar` (phase 2)

None of this is in the branch; W10's packages are tested through `internal/datasets/viewertest`, which wires them the way `cmd/hangar` should.

- **Pipeline (worker).** `pipeline.New(pipeline.Deps{DB, Blobs, Repos, LFS: <repo.LFSStore>, Jobs, MaxConvertBytes: cfg.Viewer.MaxConvertBytes.Int64(), TempDir: <data dir>/tmp, ConvertConcurrency: cfg.Viewer.ConvertConcurrency, Log})`, then `p.Register(registry)` for `dataset.convert` and `dataset.stats`, only when `viewer.enabled`.
- **Viewer (web).** `viewer.New(viewer.Deps{Repos, Authz, Store: p.Store(), Jobs, Blobs, Signer: httpx.NewSigner(<instance key>), Log, Now: time.Now}, viewer.Options{PublicURL: cfg.Server.PublicURL, MaxScanRows: int64(cfg.Viewer.MaxScanRows), MaxScanTime: cfg.Viewer.MaxScanTime, MaxCellBytes: int(cfg.Viewer.MaxCellBytes.Int64())})` (`MaxRequestBytes` defaults to the Hub's 300 MB; see §10), and `httpx.Protocols{Viewer: v.Handler()}`. The web process needs a `pipeline.Store` (`&pipeline.Store{DB: db, Blobs: blobs}`) but not the Job handlers.
- **Native API.** `api.NewDatasetsAPI(api.DatasetsDeps{Repos, Authz, Layout: &layout.Service{Repos: repos}, Store, Jobs, Log})` implements `ListDatasetConfigs` (`GET /repos/datasets/{ns}/{name}/configs`); compose it into the `gen.ServerInterface` the router serves instead of `gen.Unimplemented`.
- **Hub API (W4).** `hfapi` takes the `*viewer.Service` as its `datasets.Viewer` for `/api/datasets/{repo}/parquet[/{config}[/{split}]]` and `/api/datasets/{repo}/croissant`.
- **Retention.** `Store.DeleteOtherCommits` drops Split rows and blobs of Commits that are no longer a branch head; call it from the GC Job.

## 3. Triggers (W2, W3, W4, W6, W7)

- After the index Job of a default-branch head of a dataset (W7), and after a Mirror sync (W6), call `pipeline.EnqueueConvert(ctx, queue, repo.UUID, commit)`. It deduplicates on Repo and Commit. The Viewer also queues a head it has no rows for, so this is an optimisation, not a correctness requirement.
- `refs/convert/parquet` is written only by the pipeline, as `model.System()` with `AllowMirror: true`. W2's commit API, W3's receive-pack and W4's commit endpoint should refuse user writes to `refs/convert/*` (the Hub does). Nothing in the branch enforces it.
- For a Mirror, the pipeline adopts the upstream's own `refs/convert/parquet` when a Pull fetched it (`adoptExport`), and converts only when it is missing. W6's Pull should fetch that ref.

## 4. Index and facets (W7, W2)

- DATA-9: the index of a dataset Commit should store `meta.Summarise(card, infos)` (`internal/datasets/meta`): Configs, Splits, rows, bytes, Features, modalities, formats, task categories, languages, size category, licences and pretty name. `infos` are `Store.Info` for each Config once converted; before that the card's `size_categories` is used.
- DATA-9: for a model Commit, `meta.ModelCardDatasets(card)` gives the dataset Repo IDs of the card's `datasets` metadata, for dataset Dependencies and "models trained on this dataset".
- DATA-11: the Arsenal's dataset filters (modality, format, size category, task, language, licence) need W2's `repo.List` to filter on the stored summary. W10 has no listing code.

## 5. CLI (W9): DATA-12

`hangar pull datasets/{ns}/{name}` with `--config`, `--split` and `--parquet-only`, and `hangar datasets info`, should use `GET /api/hangar/v1/repos/datasets/{ns}/{name}/configs` for the Configs, Splits and their export status, and `Layout.Files` (through a native endpoint W9 or W2 adds, or the CLI's own copy of the selection rules) to choose files: a Config's data files plus `README.md`, or with `--parquet-only` the export paths `{config}/{split}/*.parquet`, `{config}/partial-{split}/*.parquet` and `{config}/{split}-part*/*.parquet` on `refs/convert/parquet`. W6 uses the same selection for DATA-7 and DATA-8 partial pulls.

## 6. UI (W8)

The Viewer tab reads `/datasets-server/...` and the configs endpoint: pending Splits carry the `job_id` of the conversion to follow. Media `src` URLs are signed and expire after an hour; refetch rows rather than caching them.

## 7. Documentation (W9)

Add the DuckDB note from `compat/viewer/DIFFERENCES.md` ("Client notes") to the user docs on datasets: DuckDB's `hf://` paths always go to huggingface.co (the endpoint is hard-coded in `httpfs`), so read Hangar's export with `https://{host}/datasets/{ns}/{name}/resolve/refs%2Fconvert%2Fparquet/...` URLs and an HTTP bearer secret.

## 8. Dependencies

`internal/datasets` imports `github.com/klauspost/compress` (`zstd` and `snappy`), `github.com/pierrec/lz4/v4`, `github.com/andybalholm/brotli` and `go.yaml.in/yaml/v3` directly. All were already in `go.mod` as indirect requirements of parquet-go and koanf, at the same versions, so `go.mod` is unchanged and still marks them `// indirect` until phase 2's `go mod tidy`. W10 added them to `docs/dependencies.md`. `internal/pins` can drop its blank import of parquet-go, which W10 now imports.

## 9. `scripts/fuzz.sh`: cap minimisation (integration lead)

Change: pass `-fuzzminimizetime 2000x` to `go test -fuzz`. W10 made this one-line change in its branch.

Reason: Go minimises every input that finds new coverage, for up to 60 seconds by default, and the minimiser's time grows with the square of the input's size. For `FuzzOpenAndRead` (Parquet) every new input stalled the fuzzer for the full minute, because each try snapshots the large coverage map parquet-go brings into the test binary. A 60-second run executed a few dozen inputs. With the cap, a 10-minute run executed 53 million inputs. The other fuzz targets in the repository are unaffected apart from shorter minimisation of new inputs and crashers; 2,000 tries still shrinks a crasher well. Run single targets by hand with the same flag, for example `go test -run '^$' -fuzz '^FuzzOpenAndRead$' -fuzztime 60s -fuzzminimizetime 2000x ./internal/datasets/pq`.

## 10. Configuration: the Viewer's per-request budget (phase 0 owner of `internal/config`, optional)

`viewer.Options.MaxRequestBytes` limits the decoded Parquet data one Dataset Viewer request holds, as the Hub's `rows_index.max_arrow_data_in_memory` does. Its zero value means 300 MB, the Hub's default, so the Viewer is protected without any wiring. To make it configurable, add `viewer.max_request_bytes` (a byte size, default `300MB`) to `internal/config` and pass it through in `cmd/hangar`. Conversion and statistics Jobs have no such budget: they need a memory limit in W1's Job runner (see the handoff's known gaps).
